featured_reviews.name: Ankita Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited The Outlet Many Times… and as all know it’s lot more then their Thalis… some personal recommendations here from me which surely can give a try and won’t regret….

They Have been The TIMES FOOD AWARD WINNER as well.

The Outlet is in prime location in Zaveri bazaar
Both Ac/Non -Ac Seatings available….
Quite spacious and a decent interior…
We went here for lunch on a weekday…

Their outlet speciality is the daal bati here but it’s not that up to the mark as I had expected it on my 1st visit here. So I won’t Recommend It here.
But there are some good dishes here which are worth the try.

Coming To What We Ordered….

Chaas Bottle :- 5/5
No words for it 😍😍

STARTERS :-

1. Khichiya Papad Churi :- 5/5
Quantity Of the dish perfect for 2 people. Very crunchy…not too spicy as well. Really tasted good when eaten with daal tadka and rice in main course.

2. Bhindi Fry :- 4.5/5
Really loved it mini size cut bhindi deep fried….perfect blend of spice. Surely a must have dish here. Even if deep fried it wasn’t oily which usually it turns out to be.

MAIN COURSE :-

1. Paneer Chatpata :- 5/5 ( Highly Recommended )
In Love with the dish….It was exactly as the name suggests….CHATPATA…!! Quantity really enough for 2 people. Worth the money.. Ate It with their famous butter chapati. Still not over the taste 😍😍

2. Double Daal Tadka & Rice :- 4.5/5
Daal tadka lovers a must have here.

DESSERTS :-

1. Moong Daal Ka Halwa :- 5/5 ( A Must Have Here)
Visiting Here and not having their moong daal Halwa is like your visit here is a waste….
SURELY SHOULDNT MISS OUT THIS DISH… MADE IN PURE GHEE…. not over sweet perfect sweetness… served hot and nicely garnished. DROOLWORTHY DISH.

Overall a very nice time spent here.
Food was amazing.
Service is quick.
Staff is also very much attentive and helpful.

Do check out our page on Instagram for more food suggestions @bingeandexplore page link is on my Zomato profile bio.

Firstly, I think this place hasn't been given justified reviews.. primarily because with the look, people take it as a place for LIG's to visit.
Well, I have visited enough places and exclusive South Indian ones from National Capital to all over South India..
Firstly, the hotel is 76 years old ! Yeah Circa 1953..
The layout and the marble settings you see inside is 41 years old..Yeah..they haven't changed it and trust me, it looks as good as new !
They take lot of pride in their job, making good and tasty food and feeding you..Rates are nominal for the service and for a place like 5mins in a cab from CST..
I had Butter Idli and Ghee Roast. It was very well made..as good as or better than many hifi vegetarian outlets..
If you want to a authentic..clean and good South Indian food with appreciable ambience.., you won't be disappointed..
And I said Authentic as the first expression because other places may fancy you with lights and space.. but they all tweek authenticity ! Rather quite tough to reach that spot..
So wonderful place.. Will definitely go and try some other dish next time..maybe over lunch..
They have an AC Family Room on Level 1..So, don't get discouraged with the lean trim space on Ground Floor alone..

featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Bhagat Tarachand, Kalbadevi for a team lunch and the experience was smooth and well managed.
We tried a good variety of starters including pani puri, dahi batata puri, masala khichiya papad, Harabhara kabab, kachori chaat and dahi bhalla. The dahi batata puri clearly stood out. The balance of sweet, tangy, and spicy flavors was spot on and easily the highlight of the starters.
For the main course, we ordered Peshawari tikka sabji and cheese butter masala. The cheese butter masala paired exceptionally well with cheese garlic naan, making it rich without being overpowering.
Service was prompt and efficient, which matters a lot during group lunches. The ambience is pleasant and comfortable, suitable for both team outings and family dining.
Overall, it was a satisfying dining experience with consistent food quality and good service. Definitely worth visiting if you’re around Kalbadevi.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Mao Restaurant and had an incredible dining experience! I ordered the Chicken Noorani Kabab and Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa, and I must say, the kababs were absolutely delicious. They had a delightful tandoori coating, and the filling was made of perfectly spiced seekh chicken. The spice level was just right—medium spicy, which added to the overall flavor without overwhelming the palate.

What made it even more special was that it was served on a sizzling plate, enhancing the presentation and aroma. The Chicken Tikka Mini Kepsa was a unique addition to the menu, and being the first place to serve it definitely earned them some extra points. The taste was simply amazing, and each bite was a burst of flavor.

I would highly recommend Mao Restaurant to anyone looking for a great meal. The combination of delicious food, unique offerings, and excellent presentation makes it a must-visit spot. Can't wait to go back and try more dishes!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I would never give the review or recommend this place to any one, On 17/04/2026, my friends and I visited the restaurant for dinner. After finishing our meal, we stepped outside and were waiting for a cab when one of my friends suddenly collapsed due to low blood pressure and fainted right outside your restaurant.

In that moment of urgency, I approached your staff requesting a small amount of sugar to help revive her. However, I was shocked by their response—they bluntly said they do not keep sugar. What was even more surprising was that at the same time, sugar was clearly available in the mukhwas kept there.

It was a matter of basic human kindness, and such a small help could have made a big difference in that situation. Unfortunately, the staff showed complete lack of empathy and humanity.

This is particularly disappointing because Kalbadevi has always been a place we frequently visit for lunch and dinner. Experiencing such insensitive behavior from your team was unexpected and unacceptable.

I do have a video of the incident, I will upload it soon. I will Raise a complaint too.

featured_reviews.name: Vishwesh Ranadive
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Highly Disappointing Maharashtrian Food
Overall Rating: 3/10 (Based primarily on food Taste and facilities)
My recent visit to Vinay in Girgaon was a profound disappointment, particularly for anyone seeking authentic, high-quality Maharashtrian snacks. The experience was marred by poor execution of core dishes and subpar facilities, resulting in one of the worst quick-service dining experiences I've had in a while.
The Food Verdict
The most critical failure of the visit was the Misal Pav.
• Misal Pav: 1/10
This was, quite frankly, one of the worst Misal Pavs I have ever encountered. It lacked the characteristic spice, texture, and authentic flavor profile that defines this Maharashtrian staple. It was sweet 😂. If Misal is your purpose for visiting, please look elsewhere.
• Other Dishes: 3/10 (Okish)
We also sampled the Sabudana Wada, Vatana Pattice, and Veg Biryani. While these items were merely "okish," they still scored a very low 3 out of 10. They lacked freshness, or any distinguishing quality to warrant a recommendation or even a second thought.
Ambiance and Facilities
On a positive note, the restaurant offers good sitting options, including both AC and Non-AC sections, which is a rare plus point in this category.
However, the facility challenges are severe:
• Parking: There is no dedicated parking available, which can be a significant hassle in the congested Girgaon area.
• Toilets: The washroom facilities were, without exaggeration, the worst. This is a major area needing immediate attention and upkeep.
Final Recommendation
If your goal is to experience good, authentic, and delicious Maharashtrian cuisine, do not visit Vinay. You will be better served by traveling a little further to established names.
Alternative Recommendations for Authentic Maharashtrian Food:
• Misal Pav: For a truly great Misal, visit Mamledar Misal (Thane).
• General Maharashtrian Cuisine: For excellent, reliable snacks and meals, Prakash Shuddh Upahar Kendra (Dadar) remains a gold standard.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya – A Timeless Taste of Authentic Gujarati Thali

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is one of the most iconic and beloved places to experience authentic Gujarati cuisine. Known for its traditional thali, warm hospitality, and consistent quality, this legendary eatery has earned a special place in the hearts of locals as well as visitors. Dining here feels less like eating at a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a Gujarati household.

The moment you enter Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya, you are greeted with simplicity and warmth. The interiors are modest, clean, and functional, reflecting the traditional values of Gujarati culture where food quality and hospitality matter more than luxury décor. The seating arrangement is organized, and despite the heavy rush during peak hours, the staff manages the crowd efficiently.

The highlight, without any doubt, is the Gujarati Thali. The thali is a wholesome and balanced meal that represents the true essence of Gujarat’s culinary heritage. It usually includes a variety of rotating dishes such as shaak (vegetable curries), kadhi, dal, rotli or puri, rice, khichdi, farsan, chutneys, pickles, and traditional sweets like shrikhand or mohanthal. Each item is freshly prepared and served hot.

One of the most impressive aspects of Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is the unlimited serving system. The staff continuously serves food with great attentiveness, ensuring that guests never feel rushed or restricted. The flavors are authentic—mildly spiced, well-balanced, and comforting—making the food suitable for all age groups. The use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods is clearly reflected in the taste.

Historically, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya has been serving Gujarati food for decades and is considered a cultural landmark. It has preserved the original style of Gujarati dining, where meals are meant to nourish both the body and the soul. Many regular visitors associate the place with nostalgia, family gatherings, and cultural pride.

Cleanliness and hygiene are well maintained throughout the restaurant. Plates, serving areas, and dining spaces are kept tidy, even during peak hours. The staff is polite, disciplined, and well trained, adding to the overall pleasant dining experience.

The pricing is reasonable, especially considering the quality, quantity, and authenticity of the food served. It offers excellent value for money and is often recommended as a must-visit place for anyone wanting to experience true Gujarati cuisine.

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya attracts a diverse crowd—families, elderly guests, tourists, and food lovers from across India. Despite the popularity and long waiting times during weekends, the management ensures smooth operations and quick table turnover without compromising service quality.

Overall, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is not just a restaurant but a celebration of Gujarati tradition, flavors, and hospitality. If you want to experience a soulful Gujarati thali prepared with authenticity and served with warmth, this place is an absolute must-visit. It leaves you with a satisfied heart, a happy stomach, and a deep appreciation for Gujarat’s rich culinary culture.

One of the best culinary experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. I stumbled upon this spot tucked into one of the city’s busiest, most crowded streets, and it was absolutely worth navigating the chaos to get there.

I ordered the pav bhaji and chole bhature, and both were outstanding. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced with that authentic street-style flavor, yet it felt clean and hygienic. The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene

featured_reviews.name: MONITH BISWOJYOTHI
featured_reviews.review_text:
AC hall has just 7 tables in total. We had to wait for 15mins waiting for a table. The low height of the roof surely makes walking tough for taller people (>6ft), becomes a little cramped up restaurant. Thankfully Indians aren’t that tall on average, so it’s manageable.
Coming to the food, since we didn’t want a long wait time we went with Special Thali while costs around Rs 450/-, the good thing being you can share the food. Thali was quite good, though others were going for ala-carte. The dal in thali was something special, never had seen so much of fried onions on top of dal. That’s what makes their dal thick and tasty. We also ordered Rabri and Lassi which was very thick, creamy, flavourful and worth the money paid for. The restaurant is located in the busy streets of Zaveri Bazaar (well known for 1993 Mumbai Blasts), so driving a private car is out of the question. Cabs are very difficult to get by.
